chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Shazaan ibn al-Khalil, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Al-Husayn, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man performed Wudu while wearing a turban, and removing the turban was heavy upon him due to the cold, so he said: Let him insert his finger (under the turban to wipe).
ai.seo_question: How to perform Wudu while wearing a turban if removing it is difficult due to cold?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of ease (rukhas) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits wiping the head through the turban rather than removing it entirely when cold makes removal burdensome. This ruling highlights the flexibility of the masah (wiping) requirement, allowing the finger to pass beneath the headgear to ensure the skin is touched, thereby balancing ritual purity with physical comfort.
